groups.defect: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException and the ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions calls it, so client deletion fails under V2.
ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, so token exchange fails with HTTP 500 under V2.

The management-permission accessors in ClientPermissionsV2 (isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, *Permission) throw, so the client management/permissions admin REST endpoints return 500 under V2.

answer.reasoning: There are three separate runtime defects. (1) Client deletion: s_04234c39, s_802136a9 and s_b9487ef1 all report that the ClientRemovedEvent listener calls setPermissionsEnabled, which throws, so deleting a client fails. One fix covers it. (2) Token exchange: s_4772139b and s_7789b76a both report that canExchangeTo throws during token exchange. (3) Management-permissions REST endpoints: s_886d9c42 and s_9ac2aa83 report that the permission accessors behind those endpoints throw and cause 500s. s_886d9c42 lists setPermissionsEnabled only as a method behind the endpoints and mentions the removal listener only as context, so it does not report the deletion defect. s_4772139b's 'likewise exchangeToPermission' is an aside tied to token exchange, not a report about the REST endpoints. Judge 1 merged everything by treating these side mentions as overlaps, which the rules exclude. Because the exchangeToPermission aside can be read either way, this is not fully decisive.
